content.text:
I fixed the reviewer's finding and ran `ready` again; the branch is back with the reviewer.

The reviewer was right: on mission control, a selected ready task's `⏎ open` was drawn on top of its risk chip. That's because both now sit at the right end of the task's last line. The key now goes left of the chip, with the usual gap between them, on the same line as the chip. Only mission control was affected: the board's own cards have no key, so the final board renders are unchanged.

I added the test the reviewer asked for, `the_selected_tasks_key_is_left_of_its_risks_chip_on_its_last_line`. It fails on the old placement and passes now. Rendering the reviewer's case (BP-204 selected, 160 columns) shows the key and chip side by side; that render is saved as `compare-r3/mission-160-dark-BP-204.png`.

The full suite passed again after the fix: `python3 tests/run.py` and `bin/bullpen-cargo test --workspace`. The summary file now mentions the fix and the new test.

I left the reviewer's other note alone: the `on_reviewer` dead-code warning comes from code this change doesn't touch.
